what: Rocket Lab launches small satellites on its Electron rocket, builds spacecraft and satellite components for other operators, and is developing the much larger Neutron rocket to compete for bigger payloads.
customers: Government space and defence agencies, commercial satellite operators, and prime contractors buying spacecraft components.
money: satellite manufacturing, components, solar panels and separation systems
Electron launches and, in future, Neutron
moat: The only Western company besides SpaceX with a regularly flying orbital rocket, plus a components business that supplies much of the small satellite industry.
risks: It loses money, with an operating margin around negative 38%
Neutron development is expensive and schedules in rocketry usually slip
SpaceX dominates launch economics at larger payload sizes
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
opportunities: Revenue grew about 38% last year and about 42% a year over three years
Cash of about $4.6 billion funds Neutron development without near-term dilution
Defence demand for responsive launch and satellite constellations is growing fast
watch: The Neutron first launch date and Space Systems backlog.
